# Dimensional and subgraph relations for the five-loop terminal set

Independent literature/mathematical audit, 7 October 2026. This is a research
note, not an implementation, campaign mutation, or claim that any of the
reported 829 terminals has already been eliminated. The parent investigation
is responsible for freezing and inspecting that actual terminal manifest.

## Recommendation

Do **not** make a global dimensional-shift construction the first terminal
compression pass. First project additional ordinary fixed-index IBPs onto the
existing terminal space, after exact cross-family routing and factorization.
Then investigate low-loop subgraph recurrences in clusters that resist that
pass. Dimensional shifts are useful relation generators and basis changes, but
not a universal source of extra independent fixed-d identities.

This recommendation has two unusually concrete supports:

1. A mathematical result identifies the inverse-dimensional-shift composite
   with an element of the ordinary momentum-space IBP ideal.
2. RustRed already measured a negative global-shift experiment: the two
   four-loop paired rows had 4,157 and 4,195 terms, respectively, with more than
   2,200 terms harder than the intended target. Repeating that construction
   indiscriminately for 829 five-loop targets is not justified.

The second observation is historical local evidence, not a new benchmark; see
[the measured dimensional-shortcut study](dimensional_recurrence_shortcuts_2026-10-01.md).

## 1. What dimensional recurrences really provide

Tarasov constructs dimension-changing identities through the parametric
representation and independent mass derivatives. They can trade irreducible
numerators for scalar integrals at shifted dimension. Equal masses should be
specialized **after** separate mass derivatives: differentiation in one common
mass does not reproduce every indexed raising operator. These are exact
identities in dimensional regularization, not identities obtained by declaring
the momentum vectors strictly four dimensional.
[Tarasov, hep-th/9606018](https://arxiv.org/html/hep-th/9606018).

For Euclidean vacuum normalization

\[
J_d(n)=\int\prod_{i=1}^{L}\frac{d^d k_i}{\pi^{d/2}}
          \prod_a D_a^{-n_a},\qquad
A_a f(n)=n_a f(n+e_a),\quad B_a f(n)=f(n-e_a),
\]

let \(U\) be the first Symanzik polynomial and
\(P(D)=\det(k_i\cdot k_j)\). The relevant pair is

\[
J_{d-2}=U(A)J_d,\qquad
J_{d+2}=\frac{2^L}{d(d-1)\cdots(d-L+1)}P(B)J_d.
\]

Their composition eliminates the shifted-dimensional integrals and yields
fixed-d candidate rows. The order of the operators matters; coefficients
translate under index shifts. Lee's DRA method additionally uses analyticity
to determine solutions of recurrences. It assumes IBP reduction in its setup;
it is not a replacement for discovering a small fixed-d basis.
[Lee, equations (3)–(9) and the procedure following (19)](https://arxiv.org/html/0911.0252).

### Are these fundamentally new fixed-d relations?

For the paired inverse-dimensional relation there is a precise answer:
Bitoun, Bogner, Klausen and Panzer prove in Proposition 31 that its annihilator
belongs to the shift-operator ideal generated by momentum-space IBPs. Thus it
can expose combinations missed by a bounded seed search, but does not enlarge
that full IBP ideal. Their broader comparison between all parametric
annihilators and momentum-space IBPs is posed separately, with localization
and completeness subtleties; the result must not be inflated into a theorem
that every conceivable integral identity is an ordinary IBP.
[1712.09215, Proposition 31 and Questions 23–24](https://arxiv.org/html/1712.09215).

Our inference is pragmatic: retain dimensional identities as structured
shortcut proposals or a sparse subgraph tool, not as the default explanation
for hundreds of leftover bounded-search terminals.

## 2. A sound small example and a five-loop trap

For one Euclidean massive tadpole, set \(D=k^2+m^2\), so that
\(U=A\) and \(P=B-m^2\). Composing the dimension shifts gives

\[
\bigl[2A(B-m^2)-d\bigr]J_d(n)=0,
\quad\text{hence}\quad
m^2 n J_d(n+1)=(n-d/2)J_d(n).
\]

Direct integration by parts gives precisely the same equation. There is no
new one-loop master relation hiding here. Nevertheless, if a numerical seed
search had missed that row, adding it would compress its terminal list.

At five loops the Gram relation reads

\[
P(B)J_{4-2\epsilon}
=\frac{(4-2\epsilon)(3-2\epsilon)(2-2\epsilon)
 (1-2\epsilon)(-2\epsilon)}{32}\,J_{6-2\epsilon}.
\]

Its prefactor starts at \(-3\epsilon/2\). This does **not** authorize setting
the Gram numerator to zero: the shifted integral can itself have poles, and
other reduction coefficients can contain inverse powers of epsilon. Even
when the Gram integral is evanescent, it can contribute to the desired finite
or pole coefficient after multiplication. A strict four-dimensional Gram
constraint is therefore unsafe for generic-d artifacts.

Keep dimension and epsilon symbolic during exact compression. A separate
epsilon-truncated reduction could be meaningful, but only with tracked
valuations and a rigorous required-depth budget; it would not be the same
generic artifact. The displayed coefficient is our direct specialization of
the preceding vacuum recurrence.

## 3. Subgraph integration is more promising than a global determinant

FMFT's useful structural idea is a convolution decomposition of its difficult
four-loop family into lower-loop propagator integrals. It combines local
tensor/index reductions and dimensional recurrences before the final
integration. Importantly, the paper also reports that high-numerator
dimension-shift substitutions become too long; direct negative-index
recurrences can then be preferable. It is evidence for **localized** alternate
representations, not for dimension-shift-first at all loop orders.
[FMFT, sections 2.2–2.4](https://arxiv.org/html/1707.01710).

For current five-loop terminals, the smallest sensible experiment is therefore:

1. Detect a repeated, low-loop propagator subgraph with a small separator.
2. Keep its external connector momentum symbolic.
3. Reduce that subgraph with exact identities, tracking all connector
   denominators and any new mass values.
4. Map the complete result back to the global family and existing terminals.
5. Compare the **rank of new terminal relations**, extra integral columns,
   coefficient complexity and elapsed time against ordinary seed expansion.

Reject a proposed gain that merely replaces one terminal by a new unknown
shifted-dimensional or multiscale function.

### Epsilon-dependent powers: a restricted opportunity

A massless bubble reduces to a gamma prefactor times a power of its external
momentum. A fully massive bubble instead leaves dependence on
\(m^2+x(1-x)p^2\), integrated over a Feynman parameter. It cannot in general be
replaced by one massive line with an epsilon-shifted exponent. The distinction
and explicit formulas are documented in [EPSILON.md](../../EPSILON.md).

An instructive alternative is the effective-mass method of Kniehl and
Kotikov. Their equation (8) relates otherwise retained sunset master
candidates after parameterizing a bubble and applying IBP with an effective
mass. Its published example is an on-shell, mixed-mass sunset with one
massless line; it is **not** a directly applicable identity for a fully massive
vacuum. It nevertheless supplies a concrete research template for an enlarged
subgraph representation, rather than a claim that deeper ordinary Laporta
must always find every desired relation in the initial family.
[Kniehl–Kotikov, 1202.2242](https://arxiv.org/html/1202.2242).

## 4. Relations to exhaust before expensive new algebra

### Exact routing, factorization and lower-loop reduction

Family-local terminal keys are not automatically globally distinct integrals.
An exact loop-momentum transformation must transport propagators, numerator
powers and normalization together. Graph resemblance alone is insufficient.
After such transport, a factorized block may reduce using already known
lower-loop rules.

For example, five independent massive tadpoles obey

\[
\prod_{i=1}^{5}J_d(n_i)
=J_d(1)^5\prod_{i=1}^{5}
 \frac{(1-d/2)_{n_i-1}}{(n_i-1)!}(m^2)^{1-n_i},
\qquad n_i\ge1.
\]

Many dot assignments then require only one product-master object. This
follows by iterating the explicit tadpole recurrence above; no numerical
agreement or new CAS algorithm is needed. Whether any of the 829 candidates
still has this redundancy requires the actual manifest census. Likewise,
fully massive pinches are not generically zero; scaleless free-loop or odd
integrand arguments require their own exact structural checks.

### Common-mass homogeneity: a particularly cheap candidate row

For physical propagators \(D_a=q_a^2+m^2\), positive denominator powers
\(a_a\), and a mass-independent homogeneous numerator \(N\) of momentum
degree \(2R\), dimensional scaling and differentiation of the common mass give

\[
m^2\sum_{a\in\mathrm{physical}}a_a I(a+e_a;N)
=\left(A-R-\frac{Ld}{2}\right)I(a;N),\qquad A=\sum_a a_a.
\]

This is also obtained by summing the ordinary momentum-Euler IBPs. It is not
an independent new identity, but its sparse, structured combination is cheap
to project onto a terminal set. For scalar numerators it reduces to the
familiar \(\sum a_a\)-weighted dot relation. At unit mass its mass factor is
one; the native denominator-sign convention must be translated explicitly.

Only genuine common-mass-dependent slots participate in that derivative.
A massless auxiliary ISP contributes to numerator rank but not to the mass
derivative. A negative-index auxiliary denominator containing the same mass
instead has its own derivative contribution, so its numerator is not a
mass-independent homogeneous polynomial. Either differentiate the complete
family expression, or first decompose it into genuinely homogeneous numerator
pieces. Blindly raising every slot of a complete affine family is unsafe.

This row may reduce to zero under existing rules; a newly dotted unresolved
term must be kept as an extra column. Only a nonzero exact terminal-only
remainder counts as a compression result.

### Projected ordinary Laporta

Generate ordinary IBPs at terminal-neighbor integer seeds, route every term,
and reduce every known term with the existing artifact. A nonzero remainder
among terminals is a new homogeneous terminal equation. Crucially, retain
unresolved **new** integrals as elimination columns; never drop them to force
a terminal-only relation. Eliminate the new columns first, and keep only the
resulting equations wholly in the terminal space.

This is our recommended experiment design, not a claimed new algorithm.
Finite fields can select independent rows and promising support; Symbolica
must reconstruct or perform the exact elimination, followed by exact replay.
A modular miss does not prove independence. A plateau at a seed radius does
not prove minimality. All newly retained terminals must remain explicit.

## 5. Master counts are diagnostics, not usable equations

Lee–Pomeransky relate master counting to proper critical points and Milnor
numbers; their Mint procedure assumes the relevant proper critical points are
isolated. Such geometry can prioritize a sector whose terminal count looks
too large, but it supplies neither the explicit reduction coefficients nor a
blanket certificate for a particular equal-mass, integer-index terminal list.
Symmetry identifications and special kinematics must match the count being
compared.
[1308.6676](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.6676).

Published five-loop fully massive results provide useful scale, not a target
that can be imposed by fiat. Luthe–Schroder report 103 evaluated masters for
63 sectors with five through eleven lines and explicitly leave four twelve-line
sectors outside that evaluation. Their reduction uses IBP/crusher/TIDE.
This is evidence that ordinary IBP is a credible primary compression route;
it does not prove that our 829-candidate scope must reduce to 103, or that all
its needed masters lie in that published subset.
[1609.06786, sections 2–5](https://arxiv.org/html/1609.06786).

## 6. Decision order and success criterion

| Priority | Mechanism | Evidence needed to keep it |
|---|---|---|
| First | Canonical routing, factorization, existing lower-loop reductions | Exact maps reduce distinct residual objects |
| First | Terminal-projected ordinary IBPs with adaptive integer seed shells | New replayed terminal equations at acceptable cost |
| Next | Sparse local subgraph recurrences, including dimension shifts | More terminal rank per cost than ordinary expansion |
| Diagnostic | Critical-point/master-count estimates | Correctly scoped indications of missing relations |
| Parked | Global paired Gram/Symanzik shift expansion | New evidence overcoming existing dense-row negative result |
| Unsafe | Strict d=4 Gram-zero truncation | Not admissible for the generic-d artifact |

For a frozen terminal manifest of size N, an independently verified rank-r
terminal relation matrix gives at most N-r remaining basis candidates, after
global identities already applied. Report raw, canonically routed,
factor-normalized and algebraically independent-under-found-relations counts
separately. This audit establishes promising mechanisms and a sound ordering
of experiments; it establishes no numerical decrease from 829 by itself.
